skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Access NCBI GEO gene expression datasets, metadata, SOFT files, series matrix files, and GEOparse workflows for transcriptomics analysis.
skill.summary: Find, download, parse, and analyze NCBI GEO expression datasets with Python and GEOparse.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The high static score is driven mostly by false positives in Markdown examples, public GEO URLs, placeholder API-key text, and biomedical identifiers. The only confirmed issue is the documented use of plaintext FTP for GEO downloads, which should be replaced or guarded with safer download guidance.

remediation.issue: Plaintext FTP download examples are recommended for GEO data access.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS download options when available, document integrity checks, and warn users before recursive or large downloads.

remediation.issue: The optional API key example assigns a placeholder directly in code.
remediation.suggestion: Show loading the NCBI API key from a local secret manager or environment variable, and make clear that real keys should not be committed.

remediation.issue: Examples write downloaded and derived files into local directories.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to use dedicated project directories, check available disk space, and avoid overwriting existing analysis files.

content.value_statement: Finding and preparing GEO expression datasets can be slow and error-prone. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for GEO search, download, parsing, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains GEO accession types, including GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and GEO Profiles.
Shows how to search GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles with Biopython Entrez.
Guides downloads and parsing with GEOparse for series metadata, samples, platforms, and expression matrices.
Documents direct GEO FTP paths for matrix, SOFT, MINiML, and supplementary files.
Provides example workflows for quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis.
Summarizes rate limits, citation practices, file size concerns, and common GEO data pitfalls.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a bundled executable data pipeline.
Large GEO downloads can require substantial disk space and memory.
Results depend on public GEO metadata quality and platform annotations.
Statistical examples are educational and may need review before publication use.

use_cases.title: Find relevant expression studies
use_cases.description: Search GEO by disease, organism, platform, publication date, or study type before choosing datasets.

use_cases.title: Prepare datasets for analysis
use_cases.description: Download GEO series, inspect sample metadata, and build expression matrices for downstream workflows.

use_cases.title: Compare studies across cohorts
use_cases.description: Use provided patterns for batch processing, probe mapping, and simple cross-study expression summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Search for GEO studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search NCBI GEO for human breast cancer expression studies. Include useful query terms, filters, and accession types to review.

prompt_templates.title: Download a GEO series
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a GEOparse workflow to download GSE123456, inspect sample metadata, and create an expression matrix.

prompt_templates.title: Plan differential expression
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a differential expression workflow for one GEO series with control and treatment samples. Include quality checks and multiple testing correction.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-study strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me compare TP53 expression across several GEO studies. Cover accession selection, platform mapping, batch effects, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Find GEO datasets for human diabetes RNA-seq studies.
output_examples.output: A search plan with Entrez terms, organism filters, study type filters, and accession review steps.
A GEOparse workflow outline for retrieving the series, listing samples, checking platforms, and extracting expression values.
A structured analysis plan covering dataset selection, probe annotation, normalization checks, batch effects, and citation requirements.

best_practices: Set an Entrez email and respect NCBI rate limits for every scripted request.
Inspect sample metadata, platform annotation, and processing methods before analysis.
Cache large downloads and record dataset accessions, versions, and citations.
anti_patterns: Do not assume all GEO series contain a ready-to-use series matrix file.
Do not combine studies without checking platform differences and batch effects.
Do not publish statistical results from example code without domain review.

faq.question: What databases does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on NCBI GEO DataSets, GEO Profiles, series, samples, platforms, and related file formats.

faq.question: Can it download raw and processed GEO files?
faq.answer: It explains GEOparse and direct GEO file download patterns for processed matrices, SOFT files, MINiML files, and supplementary files.

faq.question: Does it perform full statistical analysis automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and workflow guidance that should be adapted and reviewed for each study.

faq.question: Does it require an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it can increase E-utilities rate limits.

faq.question: Can it help with RNA-seq and microarray data?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers both array-based and sequence-based GEO records, but processing requirements differ by dataset.

faq.question: What should users check before trusting results?
faq.answer: Users should verify sample labels, platform annotation, normalization status, batch effects, and original study citations.
